## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Collections
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Container shape interfaces
//  - IIndexable collection interfaces
//  - IJagged (ragged row) collection interface

//==
// # Container shape interfaces
//
// The abstract data types layered over a collection: sub-ranges, concatenation,
// membership, keyed lookup, and the LIFO/FIFO disciplines. All collections are
// immutable; operations that "modify" return new collections.

// Supports taking a contiguous sub-range. Inherits ICountable so that end-relative
// helpers (Skip, TakeLast, DropLast) can convert a count into an endpoint.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Array_slicing)
//
// The range is HALF-OPEN BY ENDPOINT: [from, exclusiveTo), so the result holds
// exclusiveTo - from elements and Slice(0, Count) is the whole collection. This
// took a (start, count) pair until plato-378, which made `Slice` mean two
// different things depending on the receiver — every actual call site in the
// tree passes endpoints (`Slice(offsets[i], offsets[i+1])`), and `Array.Slice`
// was already the endpoint form. A count-based sub-range is `Array.SubArray`.
interface ISliceable
    inherits ICountable
{
    Slice(x: Self, from: Integer, exclusiveTo: Integer): Self;
}

// Supports joining two collections end to end. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concatenation)
interface IConcatenable
{
    Concat(a: Self, b: Self): Self;
}

// Supports a membership test. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_(abstract_data_type))
interface ISet<T>
{
    Contains(x: Self, item: T): Boolean;
}

// A keyed lookup collection. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associative_array)
interface IMap<TKey, TValue>
    inherits ICountable
{
    ContainsKey(x: Self, key: TKey): Boolean;
    ValueAt(x: Self, key: TKey): TValue;
}

// Last-in-first-out access. Push and Pop return new collections.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type))
interface IStack<T>
    inherits ICountable
{
    Peek(x: Self): T;
    Push(x: Self, item: T): Self;
    Pop(x: Self): Self;
}

// First-in-first-out access. Enqueue and Dequeue return new collections.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queue_(abstract_data_type))
interface IQueue<T>
    inherits ICountable
{
    Front(x: Self): T;
    Enqueue(x: Self, item: T): Self;
    Dequeue(x: Self): Self;
}

//==
// # IIndexable collection interfaces
//
// Counting, typed positions, and random access by index in one to four
// dimensions. All collections are immutable; operations that "modify" return new
// collections.

// Has a finite number of elements.
interface ICountable
{
    Count(x: Self): Integer;
}

// A typed zero-based position within an ordered collection. Value is the raw
// index; -1 means "none" / "not present". Implementors are single-field
// wrappers over Integer (VertexIndex, FaceIndex, ...), so the Value field
// satisfies this surface directly.
interface IIndex
{
    Value(x: Self): Integer;
}

// An ordered collection addressable by zero-based index.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Array_(data_structure))
interface IIndexable<T>
    inherits ICountable
{
    At(x: Self, index: Integer): T;
}

// A collection addressed by column and row (row-major count semantics).
interface IIndexable2D<T>
    inherits IIndexable<T>
{
    ColumnCount(x: Self): Integer;
    RowCount(x: Self): Integer;
    At(x: Self, column: Integer, row: Integer): T;
}

// A collection addressed by column, row, and layer.
interface IIndexable3D<T>
    inherits IIndexable<T>
{
    ColumnCount(x: Self): Integer;
    RowCount(x: Self): Integer;
    LayerCount(x: Self): Integer;
    At(x: Self, column: Integer, row: Integer, layer: Integer): T;
}

//==
// # IJagged (ragged row) collection interface
//
// The one packing seam for variable-length rows: a flat value array plus a
// boundary array. Meshes (face corners), adjacency tables, and any other list
// of lists share this shape instead of re-deriving offset arithmetic.

// A collection of variable-length rows packed in Compressed Sparse Row (CSR)
// form
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparse_matrix#Compressed_sparse_row_(CSR,_CRS_or_Yale_format)).
// Offsets has (row count + 1) entries and is non-decreasing; the items of row i
// occupy the half-open range [Offsets[i], Offsets[i+1]) of Values; the last
// offset equals Values.Count. The empty jagged collection is Offsets = [0] with
// Values = []. Offsets hold one-past-end boundaries, not element references, so
// they stay plain Integer
// (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Typed indices).
interface IJagged<T>
{
    Offsets(x: Self): Array<Integer>;
    Values(x: Self): Array<T>;
}
```
